createdBy: codex review via claude-code, T-009 round 13
impact:
An independent review of spikes/mcp/real-client/capture.mjs (codex, T-009 round 13) returned request_changes with seven findings, one critical. All are real. None can be fixed right now, and the reason is structural rather than incidental.

capture.mjs is a CAPTURE INPUT: its digest is bound into every manifest and every receipt. Editing one character invalidates all four committed captures, the gate refuses with "capture input(s) changed since the run", the derived outcome reverts from adopt-v2 to incomplete, and the tests pinned to adopt-v2 fail. Fixing any of these therefore costs a four-cell paid recapture, which requires the owner's explicit authorization and cannot be self-approved. They must be batched into ONE change and ONE recapture. ISS-057 is in the same position and should ride along.

THE RATCHET, which is the part worth noticing: the capture-input binding is what makes the evidence honest — it is why a stale capture cannot pass as current. It also means every bug found in the capture harness AFTER a capture costs money to fix, and the cost does not fall with time. Evidence that sits gets more expensive to correct, not less. That is a designed consequence, not a defect, but it should be a known one when deciding how long to leave a capture in place.

THE FINDINGS.

1. CRITICAL — appendFileSync failures are swallowed (streamRecorder.push). writeErrors and totalBytes are incremented and never read. A transient write failure omits a chunk from the retained transcript while the capture continues; the digest is then taken from the FILE, so it authenticates an incomplete stream, while the disclosure predicates are computed from the in-memory copy that still holds the chunk. The receipt reproduces the digest and accepts it. Paid raw evidence is destroyed silently and the retained file is misrepresented as the complete stream. Fix: fail closed when writeErrors is nonzero or the file size differs from totalBytes; record a typed recording failure and forbid sanitization or receipt creation for that attempt.

2. MAJOR — cleanup() runs before the post-run checkpoint and can throw. A filesystem cleanup failure skips checkpoint(), rejects captureCell(), and prevents noteAttempts() from ever associating the already-paid capture with cells.json. The same exposure exists at the final classify() call, after derivation succeeded but before captureCell returns. Fix: checkpoint the exit state BEFORE cleanup, catch cleanup failures without discarding the result, and persist a classification failure rather than throwing.

3. MAJOR — drainTimedOut is recorded and enforced by nothing. VERIFIED: classify.mjs never reads the field. When the post-kill drain deadline expires, descendants may still be writing the files the harness is about to hash, so the digests do not describe a settled state — the manifest's own comment says exactly this — yet the capture can still classify as a pass and be receipted. This is the recurring shape yet again: a fact recorded without an enforcer. Fix: make drainTimedOut a fail-closed classifier condition.

4. MAJOR — the ownership marker is checked with existsSync, so ANY filesystem object named spendbar-t009-capture satisfies it: a directory, a symlink, an empty file someone else wrote. Combined with a capture-shaped directory name, an unrelated directory is recursively deleted inside the operator's home. The stated invariant is that the sweep only deletes what it can prove it wrote, and existsSync does not prove that. Fix: lstat the marker, require a non-symlink regular file, and require its contents to equal the directory's captureId — which is exactly what captureCell writes.

5. MAJOR — the CI marker list is not an enforcement boundary. CIRCLECI, TRAVIS, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER and TEAMCITY_VERSION are missing, and any runner that clears the known variables passes. Fix: add the missing markers, and DOCUMENT the list as defense in depth rather than the boundary. The reviewer also proposed requiring an interactive TTY confirmation. That is deliberately NOT adopted: this command is legitimately driven non-interactively by an agent session — both authorized recaptures were — and a TTY gate would have blocked them while stopping no real CI run that had the variables cleared.

6. MAJOR — an attempt reaches cells.json only after captureCell returns, so any interruption between the paid client starting and that return leaves the captureId unrecorded and its receipt unassociable. Overlaps 2, but the complete fix is larger: generate the captureId before the call, journal an in-progress attempt atomically before spawning, finalize after return, and have startup report unfinished journal entries instead of starting another paid capture.

7. MAJOR — privacy leak through an error path. The catch around sanitize/checkPreservation also covers writeFileAtomic, and copies error.message into cells.json, which is COMMITTED. Filesystem errors routinely carry absolute paths, so a failed rename or open commits the operator's username and repository path. The derivation handler two blocks earlier already avoids this by recording only an error class; this one does not. Fix: commit a fixed sanitized cause and send the detail to local stderr only.
title: Seven capture-harness defects found after the evidence was captured — all fixable only by spending another four-cell recapture
